newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Southam returns to profit in 4th quarter.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Southam returns to profit in 4th quarter.

text.p: Southam Inc., Canada's largest daily newspaper publisher and the newest addition to the empire of press baron Conrad Black, said on Wednesday it returned to profitability in the fourth quarter of 1996.
Southam earned C$36.8 million ($27 million) or C48 cents (36 cents) a share in the quarter, including a pre-tax gain of C$5.5 million ($4 million) from an asset sale.
That contrasted with a year-earlier loss of C$58.1 million ($43 million) or C77 cents (57 cents) a share in the same quarter.
Sales at the newspaper group rose 19.1 percent to C$273.5 million ($201 million) in the fourth quarter and Southam said about two-thirds of the increase was due to acquisitions.
Southam's 1995 loss was due to a C$120 million ($88 million) pre-tax charge, tied mainly to job cuts in the company's newspaper division and an asset writedown.
For the full 1996 year, Southam earned C$94 million ($69.6 million), or C$1.23 (91 cents) a share, versus a 1995 loss of C$53.4 million ($39.5 million), or C70 cents (52 cents) a share.

Black, chief executive of Southam since the departure of William Ardell last year, also owns or has a stake in such newspapers as London's Daily Telegraph, the Jerusalem Post and the Chicago Sun-Times. Southam papers in Canada include the Ottawa Citizen and the Montreal Gazette.
Black's Hollinger Inc. last year more than doubled its Southam stake to 50.1 percent in two transactions.
Black took control of Southam after voicing irritation with the Toronto-based company's poor results and what he called "an obdurate rump of continuing Southam directors."
Soon afterward, Black ousted several directors. In the following months, several executives including Ardell, and some Southam editors and publishers also left the company.
